intro: Saints are friends in heaven who pray for us and show us how to follow Jesus. Many people choose a patron saint, especially for confirmation. Pick what draws you, and see who matches.

interests.label: Came to faith as an adult
Migrants and people far from home

saints.name: St. Augustine of Hippo
saints.story: A brilliant teacher who spent his youth chasing pleasure and success. After years of searching, he was baptized at 32 and became a bishop and one of the Church's greatest thinkers. He wrote: "Our heart is restless until it rests in you."

saints.name: St. Monica
saints.story: Augustine's mother, who prayed for her son for many years and lived to see him baptized. A model of persevering prayer for loved ones.

saints.name: St. Mary Magdalene
saints.story: A follower of Jesus whom he freed from seven demons. She stayed at the cross and was the first to see the risen Lord, who sent her to tell the apostles.

saints.name: St. Peter
saints.story: A fisherman Jesus called to be the rock of his Church. He denied Jesus three times, was forgiven, and gave his life for him in Rome.

saints.name: St. Paul
saints.story: Once a persecutor of Christians, he met the risen Jesus on the road to Damascus and became the great apostle to the nations. His letters fill much of the New Testament.

saints.name: St. Teresa Benedicta of the Cross (Edith Stein)
saints.story: A Jewish-born philosopher who lost her faith, then found Christ after reading the life of St. Teresa of Ávila in one night. She became a Carmelite nun and was killed at Auschwitz.

saints.name: St. Elizabeth Ann Seton
saints.story: A New York wife and mother of five who became Catholic as a young widow, despite opposition from family and friends. She founded schools and a religious community, and was the first saint born in the United States. Her feast, January 4, is kept in the United States but is not on the Canadian calendar.

saints.name: St. Josephine Bakhita
saints.story: Kidnapped as a child in Sudan and sold into slavery, she was eventually brought to Italy, where she found freedom and faith. Baptized as an adult, she became a sister known for her gentleness and forgiveness.

saints.name: St. Kateri Tekakwitha
saints.story: A Mohawk woman who was baptized at 20 despite hostility from her community. She moved to the Christian village of Kahnawake, near Montreal, where she lived a life of deep prayer, and her tomb is there today. She was the first Indigenous saint of North America. In Canada her feast is April 17.

saints.name: St. Thérèse of Lisieux
saints.story: A young French Carmelite nun who taught the "Little Way": doing small, ordinary things with great love. She died at 24 and is a Doctor of the Church.

saints.name: St. Francis of Assisi
saints.story: A rich young man who gave everything away to follow Jesus in poverty, joy and love for all creation. He founded the Franciscans.

saints.name: St. Teresa of Calcutta
saints.patron: the Missionaries of Charity, World Youth Day
saints.story: Known as Mother Teresa, she served the poorest of the poor in India and around the world, seeing Jesus in each person.

saints.name: St. Joseph
saints.story: The husband of Mary and foster father of Jesus. A quiet, faithful carpenter who protected the Holy Family.

saints.name: St. John Paul II
saints.story: A Polish actor, poet and athlete who became pope in 1978. He loved young people, started World Youth Day, and taught that "the future of humanity passes by way of the family."

saints.name: St. Thomas Aquinas
saints.story: A Dominican friar and one of the greatest thinkers in history, who showed that faith and reason work together.

saints.name: St. Pier Giorgio Frassati
saints.story: A joyful Italian student who loved mountain climbing, friends and the poor, whom he served in secret. He died at 24 and was canonized in 2025.

saints.name: St. Carlo Acutis
saints.story: An Italian teenager who loved video games, coding and the Eucharist. He built a website about Eucharistic miracles and died of leukemia at 15. He was canonized in 2025.

saints.name: St. Gianna Beretta Molla
saints.story: An Italian doctor, wife and mother who loved skiing and the mountains. During a difficult pregnancy she chose to protect her child's life, and died shortly after her daughter's birth.

saints.name: St. Luke
saints.story: A physician and companion of St. Paul who wrote the Gospel of Luke, including the road to Emmaus, and the Acts of the Apostles.

saints.name: St. Cecilia
saints.story: An early Roman martyr remembered for singing to God in her heart. She is the patron of music and musicians.

saints.name: St. Maximilian Kolbe
saints.story: A Polish Franciscan priest and publisher who, at Auschwitz, offered to die in place of a father of a family.

saints.name: St. André Bessette
saints.patron: the sick, St. Joseph's Oratory in Montreal
saints.story: An orphan from Quebec with little schooling and poor health, he became a Holy Cross brother and worked for decades as a doorkeeper. He welcomed the sick, prayed with them and sent them to St. Joseph, and many were healed. His trust in St. Joseph built St. Joseph's Oratory on Mount Royal in Montreal.

saints.name: St. Marguerite Bourgeoys
saints.story: A Frenchwoman who crossed the ocean to the small settlement that became Montreal. She opened its first school in a stable, taught girls and families, and founded the Congregation of Notre-Dame, one of the first uncloistered communities of sisters in North America.

saints.name: St. Marguerite d'Youville
saints.story: Born in Quebec, she suffered an unhappy marriage and was widowed young with children to raise and debts to pay. She turned her grief into love for the poor, took in the sick and abandoned in Montreal, and founded the Grey Nuns. She was the first saint born in Canada.

saints.name: St. John de Brébeuf and the Canadian Martyrs
saints.story: A French Jesuit who lived among the Huron-Wendat people in what is now Ontario. He learned their language, wrote the Huron Carol, one of Canada's oldest Christmas songs, and was martyred with his companions. The Canadian Martyrs are secondary patrons of Canada.

saints.name: St. Frances Xavier Cabrini
saints.story: An Italian sister who crossed the ocean to serve Italian immigrants in the United States, founding schools, orphanages and hospitals. Her feast, November 13, is kept in the United States but is not on the Canadian calendar.
